newsitem.title: USA: Pinnacle West says lower rates hit earnings.
newsitem.headline: Pinnacle West says lower rates hit earnings.

text.p: Pinnacle West Capital Corp, parent of Arizona Public Service Co (APS), said Wednesday the utility's second quarter earnings were hurt by a decrease in regulated rates for electricity customers.

But results from the company's non-utility operations, lower interest expenses and a stock buyback program, helped lift overall earnings for the quarter to 79 cents a share from 67 cents in the same 1996 period, Pinnacle West said.
Results for the second quarter of 1996 included a three-cent-per-share extraordinary charge, after tax, for debt prepayment penalties.
Chairman Richard Snell said results in the latest quarter reflect strong ongoing fundamentals, including customer growth at APS and greater efficiency throughout the company.

Under a July 1996 agreement with the Arizona Corporation Commission, APS reduced electricity rates by 3.4 percent and accelerated amortization of regulatory assets, which together reduced after-tax earnings for the second quarter of this year by around 29 cents a share, the company said.

Snell said that under the agreement a second price decrease became effective July 1, 1997 and will affect earnings going forward. The $17.6 million or 1.2 percent price reduction is APS' third decrease in as many years.
